correctness.rationale: The Walsh operator action yields eigenvalues J(d-2k)+K(-1)^k. The minimal parity representatives k=d,d-1 are compared exactly for every real K/J; the Rayleigh bound is attained by sign characters. The key rigidity lemma is established by a complete square-Walsh coefficient comparison, proving every sign-valued element of the lowest eigenspace is a single character. Pair correlations follow by an exact count of coordinate disagreements. A standalone exhaustive enumerator tested all spin assignments for d=2,3,4 at 11 couplings each (723888 total assignments), all 132 distance correlations, and the full Walsh spectrum for 35 further cases through d=8. The finite checks are not substituted for the all-d proof.

originality.rationale: The complete all-dimensional minimizer/equality classification and exact piecewise correlation law for separately weighted distance-one and antipodal bonds were not found in inspected primary literature or source-record searches. The two-domain spin pattern and spectral-bound methods are explicitly preexisting and credited; neither the Franco–Cannas fixed Hamming-shell model nor the general Hamming-scheme eigenvalue bound implies the stated tunable two-shell classification without new Boolean equality reasoning. Historical priority remains subject to independent specialist review.
residual_risks: No independent priority review; obscure earlier exact weighted folded-cube max-cut or spin-correlation classification may exist.
The 2010 folded-hypercube graph PDF was only partially visually inspected (six of eight pages); findings about unread pages are not asserted.
The coincidence of the 2d opposed-domain ground-state pattern with Franco–Cannas (2003) is known, even though the Hamiltonian and continuum of couplings differ.
Known general spectral bounds strongly inform the energy proof; originality rests on the complete coupling/equality/correlation classification, not on rediscovering Walsh diagonalization.

value.rationale: This is an all-d exact finite frustrated-spin classification on the canonical cube plus antipodal matching, with a tunable physical exchange, a sharp parity-selected crossing, provably exhaustive degeneracies and exact distance-correlation changes. It isolates a natural spectral degeneracy/equality mechanism, rather than an arbitrary tiny instance or a bare normalization check. It does not assert a bulk thermal phase transition.
